prompt: A farmer tests $H_0$: the new fertilizer does not change mean yield, against $H_a$: the new fertilizer increases mean yield. Which describes a Type I error in this context?

choices.label: Concluding the fertilizer increases yield when it really does not.
Concluding the fertilizer does not increase yield when it really does.
Using a sample that is too small to detect any change.
Correctly concluding the fertilizer increases yield.

hint: Type I error: rejecting $H_0$ when $H_0$ is actually true — a "false alarm".

hints.text: Type I error: rejecting $H_0$ when $H_0$ is actually true — a "false alarm".
Rejecting $H_0$ here means declaring the fertilizer works. A Type I error is doing that when it does not.
A: the farmer concludes the fertilizer increases yield, but in reality it does not.

explanation: A Type I error happens when $H_0$ is true but we reject it. Here $H_0$ true means the fertilizer does nothing.
Rejecting $H_0$ means concluding the fertilizer increases yield. Doing so when it does not is the Type I error: choice A.
B is a Type II error (missing a real effect). C is a design weakness, not an error type. D is a correct decision.

alternativeExplanations.title: False alarm vs. missed alarm
steps: Type I = false alarm: we shout "it works!" and it does not. The farmer buys useless fertilizer.
Type II = missed alarm: it works, but we say "no evidence." The farmer misses a real gain.
The question asks for the false alarm: A.
